title: Bear on, My Soul! the Bitter Cross
description: Bear on, My Soul! the Bitter Cross in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 532, “Through Cross to Light”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bear on, my soul! the bit-ter cross Of ev-ery tri-al here Shall lift thee to thy heaven a-bove, But shall not en-ter there.

lines: Bear on, my soul! the bitter cross
Shall lift thee to thy heaven above,
Bear on, my soul! on God rely;
A thousand ways the Father hath
And Thou, my heavenly Friend and Guide,
Taught me to rest my fainting head

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
